parts.latex: Which of the following is equivalent to the true bearing of $250^\circ$?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{497_q9_s1}

A true bearing of $250^\circ$ is measured clockwise from north.

Since $180^\circ < 250^\circ < 270^\circ$, the direction lies between south and west.

It is past south by
$$250^\circ - 180^\circ = 70^\circ$$
towards the west, so the direction is $\text{S}70^\circ\text{W}$.

Options A and C are not valid compass-bearing forms, and $\text{S}20^\circ\text{E}$ is $160^\circ$.
$$\therefore\ \text{S}70^\circ\text{W (option D)}$$

497_q9_s1.notes: New sketch drawn from the worked solution. O at the centre with labels N (solid north line), S, E and W (dashed). The ray at bearing 250° (S70°W) goes into the SW quadrant. The outer clockwise arc with an arrowhead runs from N to the ray, labelled 250°. The inner clockwise arc runs from N to S, labelled 180°. A small arc between S and the ray is labelled 70°. In round 2 the arc radii were enlarged so that every label sits clear of the arcs and lines. Rules 3, 4, 11, 14, 22.

parts.latex: The bearing from $O$ to $P$ is $S57^\circ E$. Which is the compass bearing to $O$ from $P$?

solutions.latex:
From $O$, the point $P$ lies $57^\circ$ east of south.

The return direction from $P$ to $O$ is exactly opposite: north becomes south and east becomes west, with the same angle.

So the bearing from $P$ to $O$ is $N57^\circ W$.

The question asks for the compass bearing, so the answer is $N57^\circ W$ (the equivalent true bearing is $303^\circ$, but that is not in compass form).

Hence the answer is option B.

meta.self_check: Reverse of S57E is N57W = 360-57 = 303 true bearing; compass-form option is B.

parts.latex:
Town $B$ is 45 km due north of town $A$ and 30 km from town $C$. Town $A$ is 39 km from town $C$.

Not to Scale

\exfigure{2839_q4a_1}

What is the bearing of town $C$ from town $B$?

solutions.latex:
In triangle $ABC$, use the cosine rule to find $\angle CBA$:
$$\begin{aligned}\cos B &= \dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2ac} \\ &= \dfrac{30^2+45^2-39^2}{2\times 30\times 45} \\ &= \dfrac{13}{25} \\ \angle CBA &= 58.66\ldots^\circ\end{aligned}$$
BA points due south from $B$ (bearing $180^\circ$), and $C$ is further round, so
$$\text{bearing} = 180^\circ + 58.66\ldots^\circ = 239^\circ \text{ (to the nearest degree)}$$
This is option C.

Lines 0.6pt, house aux dashes with a filled Latex head (rules 3, 4). Round 2 reduced the labels to \scriptsize to match the printed size (rule 2). All labels are clear of the lines (rule 11).

figures.cap: towns A, B, C with north line and 48 degree angle

solutions.latex:
The $48^\circ$ at $A$ is measured from due south ($AC$), so the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is
$$180^\circ - 48^\circ = 132^\circ$$
The bearing of $A$ from $B$ is the reverse direction.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } A \text{ from } B &= 132^\circ + 180^\circ \\ &= 312^\circ \end{aligned}$$
So the correct option is D.

6269.stem:
Two hikers decide to leave a campsite ($C$) to visit some landmarks in the area. One hiker walks 26 km on a bearing of $065^\circ$T to see a lake ($L$), the other hiker walks 16 km on a bearing of $285^\circ$T to see a mountain ($M$).

\exfigure{496_q32_1}

figures.cap: campsite C with bearings to lake L and mountain M

parts.latex: Calculate the distance between the Mountain ($M$) and the Lake ($L$), correct to the nearest kilometre.

Hence, find the bearing of the lake from the mountain.

Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
The angle is made up of the bearing $065^\circ$ and the angle from north back to $285^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle MCL &= 65 + (360 - 285) \\ &= 65 + 75 \\ &= 140^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Let $x = ML$. Using the cosine rule in $\triangle MCL$:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 16^2 + 26^2 - 2(16)(26)\cos 140^\circ \\ &= 256 + 676 - 832\cos 140^\circ \\ &= 1569.34897\ldots \\ x &= 39.61500\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{distance} \approx 40 \text{ km}$$
criteria: Substitutes into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $C$ from $M$ is the reverse of $285^\circ$, but measured from the north at $M$ it is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{bearing of } C \text{ from } M &= 90 + 15 \\ &= 105^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Let $\theta = \angle CML$. Using the sine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin\theta}{26} &= \dfrac{\sin 140^\circ}{39.615\ldots} \\ \theta &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{26\sin 140^\circ}{39.615\ldots}\right) \\ &= 24.95\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{bearing from } M \text{ to } L &= 105 - 25 \\ &= 080^\circ \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the angle $CML$, or equivalent merit
Finds the bearing of $C$ from $M$, or equivalent merit
